newsitem.title: India: Bombay shares erase losses, index crosses 3000 pts.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares erase losses, index crosses 3000 pts.

text.p: ** Bombay shares rebound sharply on Monday after plunging nearly four percent in early trade
** Bombay's benchmark stocks index ended 35.44 points higher at a provisional 3001.10 after hitting an early low of 2856.21
** Shares of ITC rebound near close on rumours the firm's first half net will be above market expectations at around 1.8 billion rupees
** Auto stocks hit as funds offload on fears of prolonged slowdown in economy
Bombay shares rebounded sharply at close on Monday erasing large, early losses, traders said.
They said shares were pounded lower in early trade as foreign funds sold on an onslaught of disappointing first half results and on fears of a prolonged slowdown in the economy.
But prices rebounded in late trade as punters rushed to cover short positions after prices fell nearly four percent.
Bombay's benchmark stocks index plunged 109.45 points or 3.7 percent to an early low of 2856.21. It erased all losses to end 35.44 points up at a provisional 3001.10.
"Speculators got nervous after the index tumbled below 2900 points and buying support from some local funds made them rush for cover," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.

They said rumours that first half results of index-linked stock ITC were likely to be above market expectations at around 1.8 billion rupees ($50.4 million) had also driven prices higher. ITC results are due later in the day.
A series of disappointing results for the six months to September 1996 announced last week have depressed sentiment. The index fell five percent in the week to Friday.
Auto stocks -- previously the darlings of foreign funds -- have been worst hit by fears of a prolonged economic slowdown.
"The initial bull run which was led by auto stocks has come a full circle," said Partha Roy Choudhary, head of trading at securities firm Peregrine Capital.
India's April-September industrial growth has slowed to 4.8 percent from 12.8 percent during the corresponding period last year, according to official data released last week.
Auto analysts say a slowdown in demand has resulted in rising inventories which will translate into lower sales in the second half of 1996/97 (April-March).
